Fine. Count up to n for n maybe "0" or negative. count_good_numbers_between calls count_good_numbers_up_to(str(int(a)-1)). If a=1, str(0)="0". dfs handles. For num1 >=1. If tight true, limit=n[pos], tight and digit==limit; correct. Memoization includes tight so correct.

Response B brute force from num1 to n; impossible for huge. Also count_good_integers_up_to uses int(num1) rather than range start? For n maybe less than num1 but not. It loops from num1 to n. Then result = up_to(num2)-up_to(num1-1). up_to(num1-1) loops range(num1,num1) zero. So counts from num1 to num2. It would be mathematically correct but infeasible and constraints huge; not acceptable. In programming judge correctness includes efficient. A is correct.
